layout.notes: Two page grids (p1, p2), same columns, one block each. Header labels are offset from data: the 'Area (sq ft)' header is in D but values are in E; 'Rent AED' header is in K but values are in L (the TOTAL row on p2 puts the rent total in K52 and the area total in E52). Area header says sq ft but values (studio 43.0, 1BR ~70, 2BR ~111-116) are clearly sq m; the total 8,302.5 over 105 units agrees. Rent is annual AED (1BR about 90-105k). Long tenant names wrap onto extra lines: a tenant fragment in column F sits on its own row above the unit row and the remainder on its own row below it (e.g. p1 F7 'Alder Horizon Software Development' + F9 'L.L.C' belong to unit 104 in row 8). These wrap rows have no unit number and are excluded; the unit row has an empty tenant cell in those cases, so the tenant is the concatenation of the row above and the row below. Vacant rows have no rent, tenant or dates. Some occupied rows lack an Ejari number. Chq column is the number of cheques. Column A is a running serial number. Page footers and the 'Synthetic document' line are not units. No remarks column.

opex.notes: Footnote: "Expenses include VAT at 5% (not recoverable)." VAT status of income is not stated. No vacancy/collection loss or district cooling lines appear on the statement; none invented.

discrepancies.title: Rent roll totals do not equal the sum of its rows: annual rent

sources.label: sum of unit rows: annual rent

discrepancies.why: The stated total is not the sum of the unit rows (it may be stale or typed over). The screen re-sums the rows and ignores the stated totals.

impact.basis: sum of rows minus stated total

discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask the property manager for a system export of the rent roll at the same date.

discrepancies.title: 83.9% of in-place rent expires between 2027-01-31 to 2027-04-29

sources.label: leases ending 2027-01-31 to 2027-04-29 (rent roll lease end dates)

discrepancies.why: A cluster of expiries means one leasing season sets most of the income, in a falling market. The mandate limit is 40.0% in any 3-month window of the 12 months from 2026-10-31.
discrepancies.analyst_action: Ask for the renewal status and notices on the expiring leases; consider a price holdback or rent guarantee.

discrepancies.title: 4 let unit(s) with no Ejari number (705, 1103, 1301, 1304)
discrepancies.why: A tenant holding over on an expired or unregistered lease has a weaker legal position for the landlord (an unregistered contract lacks legal standing). The engine rolls expired leases at the start of the analysis; AED 412,000 of in-place rent (3.9%) sits on these units.

impact.basis: in-place rent on the affected units

discrepancies.analyst_action: Request Ejari certificates and renewal status for each listed unit.

notices.text: Cheque profile: 49% of rent on 1-2 cheques, 32% of rent on 3-4 cheques, 19% of rent on 6 or more cheques. More cheques mean more collection risk and less post-dated cheque cover.
Statement NOI moved -0.3% against the prior period (12 months to Sep 2025).

diligence_checklist.text: Title deed and DLD ownership search: freehold status, single title, and that the buyer is eligible to own the plot.
Building completion certificate (Dubai Municipality) for the as-built building.
Affection plan and permitted use: confirm residential use and the plot's permitted floors match the building.
Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
Civil Defence completion and annual fire-safety certificates, and ACP cladding compliance.

memo.markdown:
## Verdict
**Needs work**: the building passes the hard mandate filters but misses the soft tests on going-in yield, unlevered IRR, equity multiple and lease expiry concentration.

Buy at AED 99.9m [[uw.walk_away_price_aed]], exit at 6.2% [[uw.exit_yield]]. That is 35% below asking [[uw.walk_away_vs_asking]], against an asking price of AED 152.5m [[deal.asking_price_aed]]. The exit yield moves the walk-away price most: 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] either way moves it by AED 14.7m [[uw.walk_away_largest_swing_aed]]. The walk-away price and returns rest on the firm's house view (reference rent path, exit yield, vacancy and downtime), not on market evidence for this building.

## The deal
- **What and where:** Corvina Tower, Business Bay (Bay Avenue side), 105 units [[om.unit_count]], completed 2025 [[deal.completion_year]]. Freehold, single title.
- **Price:** asking AED 152.5m [[deal.asking_price_aed]], AED 1,706 per sq ft [[uw.price_per_sqft_nsa]] on NSA.
- **Income:** in-place rent AED 10.7m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]], 95% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] occupied by units. All direct leases, no master tenant. Tenants pay chiller.

## Returns
Unlevered, pre-tax:

| Metric | Result | Mandate |
|---|---|---|
| Unlevered IRR | 3.4% [[uw.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]] | 7.5% [[mandate.target_unlevered_irr.threshold]] target |
| Equity multiple | 1.16x [[uw.unlevered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]] | 1.30x [[mandate.target_unlevered_equity_multiple.threshold]] target |
| Going-in net yield on total cost | 5.3% [[uw.going_in_net_yield_on_cost]] | 6.0% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]] minimum |
| Entry yield on price | 5.7% [[uw.entry_yield_on_price]] | none |
| Exit yield | 6.2% [[uw.exit_yield]] | none |

Year-1 NOI is AED 8.7m [[uw.noi_year1]]. Levered IRR is 1.6% [[uw.levered_irr_pre_tax]] and the levered multiple 1.08x [[uw.levered_equity_multiple_pre_tax]]. Year-1 DSCR is 1.40x [[uw.dscr_year1]].

The OM headlines a net yield of 5.6% [[om.yield_stated]] on total cost. On the buyer's basis (Year-1 NOI on price plus acquisition costs) it is 5.3% [[uw.om_yield.buyer_net_on_total_cost]], 0.2 points [[uw.om_yield.gap_vs_stated]] lower.

## What would make it fail
- **Exit yield.** With the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] wider, unlevered IRR is 2.1% [[uw.sens.r+0.e+50.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]]. With market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] lower as well, it is 0.8% [[uw.sens.r-5.e+50.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]], and levered IRR is a loss of 2.3% a year [[uw.sens.r-5.e+50.levered_irr_pre_tax]].
- **No upside case reaches the target.** With market rent 5% [[uw.sens.rent_shift_step]] higher and the exit yield 50 bps [[uw.sens.exit_shift_step_bps]] tighter, unlevered IRR is 6.1% [[uw.sens.r+5.e-50.unlevered_irr_pre_tax]], still under the 7.5% [[mandate.target_unlevered_irr.threshold]] target.
- **Expiry cliff.** 84% [[uw.max_expiry_share_quarter]] of in-place rent, AED 8.9m [[uw.max_expiry_window_rent_aed]], expires between 31 January 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_start]] and 29 April 2027 [[uw.max_expiry_window_end]]. The mandate limit is 40% [[mandate.max_lease_expiry_share_in_any_quarter.threshold]]. The house view has market rents falling 3.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1.

## Discrepancies
Most severe first. No lower-severity items are discussed.
1. **Rent roll totals do not equal the sum of its rows (high).** The stated annual rent total is not the sum of the unit rows, and may be stale or typed over. The screen re-summed the unit rows and ignored the stated totals. Impact: the stated totals cannot be relied on until a system export confirms them.
2. **Lease expiry concentration (high).** Most of the rent resets in one leasing season, as set out above. The screen relied on the rent roll. Impact: one season sets most of the income, in a falling rent path.
3. **Let units with no Ejari number (medium).** 4 [[disc.expired_lease_counted_occupied.title]] let units have no Ejari number. AED 412,000 [[disc.expired_lease_counted_occupied.why]] of in-place rent (3.9% [[disc.expired_lease_counted_occupied.why]]) sits on them. The screen rolls them as expired at the start of the analysis. Impact: a weaker legal position for the landlord on these tenants.

## Checks before diligence
- Get a system export of the rent roll at the same date from the property manager.
- Get renewal status and notices on the expiring leases. Consider a price holdback or rent guarantee.
- Get Ejari certificates and renewal status for each unit without an Ejari number.
- Cheque profile: about half of rent is on one or two cheques, and about a fifth on six or more. More cheques mean more collection risk.
- Statement NOI is slightly down on the prior period.
- Title deed and DLD ownership search: freehold, single title, buyer eligibility.
- Building completion certificate.
- Affection plan and permitted use.
- Ejari export for every lease, reconciled to the rent roll.
- Civil Defence certificates and cladding compliance.

## Assumptions
Exit yield is 6.2% [[uw.exit_yield]], including 25 bps [[assume.exit_yield_expansion_bps]] of expansion. Market rent falls 3.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year1]] in Year 1 and 1.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year2]] in Year 2. It then rises 2.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year3]], 3.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year4]] and 3.0% [[assume.rent_growth_year5]]. Structural vacancy is 5.0% [[assume.structural_vacancy]] and collection loss 1.0% [[assume.collection_loss]]. The loan is AED 57.0m [[uw.loan_aed]] (37% [[uw.ltv]] LTV, 6.8% [[uw.interest_rate]] rate). It is sized to cover Year-1 NOI at 1.40x [[assume.sizing_dscr]]. No operating cost categories were filled from mandate defaults.
